Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — quick background: DataPriv is finalizing an agreement with Redwood for inference hosting and we need to validate your international transfer posture before legal signs off. Our procurement checklist specifically asks for:

- Confirmation you support the EU Commission SCCs (2021) for controller->processor transfers and the UK IDTA / UK Addendum for UK-controlled data.
- The current subprocessors list and whether any subprocessors store non-PII logs or customer identifiers in the US.
- Whether you are willing to sign a TIA/DTIA addendum (our security team calls it a Technical Impact Assessment) or provide equivalent technical mitigations in writing.
- A redline or your standard DPA and an estimated timeline to execute (DocuSign preferred).

Can you send the SCC/UK addendum mapping and your current DPA redline? Also let us know if you require any changes to our draft.

Appreciate a reply by EOD Wednesday if possible — Aisha

Hi Aisha — Neha from Redwood Legal here.

Thanks for the checklist; a couple of clarifications and a proposed path forward below.

Summary: Redwood will sign the EU SCCs (2021) incorporated into our DPA and the UK IDTA / UK Addendum where UK personal data is in scope. For US transfers we rely on SCCs plus technical/evidentiary supplementary measures as required by guidance — we document those in the DTIA annex.

Steps we recommend:
1) Confirm scope: controller vs controller+processor fields in your draft. If DataPriv is the controller and Redwood the processor, we proceed with Redwood as Processor under the SCCs + UK Addendum.
2) Subprocessors: we will provide our current subprocessors spreadsheet and indicate which subprocessors may store metadata or logs in the US. Most production inference traffic stays in-region; only analytics and centralized logging (obfuscated) cross into US-hosted services.
3) DTIA/TIA: we can provide a DTIA addendum that includes:
   - Encryption at rest (AES-256) for persisted customer data;
   - TLS 1.2+ in transit;
   - Role-based access, least privilege, and restricted break-glass processes;
   - Key management details and KMS options for Dedicated/Private deployments.
4) Timeline: we can push the DPA + SCCs + UK Addendum for signature within 3 business days after you confirm minor redlines. More substantive changes may require legal review (5-7 business days).

Attachments: I attached a redlined DPA (same as Marissa’s) and a suggested clause text for the UK Addendum.

Open items for your security team:
- Do you require certificate-based key custody or customer-managed keys?
- Is logging telemetry considered personal data for your purposes (then we’ll need to confirm retention periods and masking)?

If helpful we can provide our SOC 2 Type II summary and set up an engineer call for DTIA specifics. Happy to join the call Marissa proposed on Wednesday.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
